---
title: Any language
description: Use ClipMux from Python, Go, PHP, Ruby or any backend with its REST API, an API key and two small pieces of tested code.
---

There is a server SDK for Node only, but nothing in ClipMux needs it. Your
backend makes three kinds of call, and each works from any language:

- **REST calls** with an API key, to create uploads and read videos.
- **Signing playback tokens**, locally, with your app's signing key.
- **Verifying webhooks**, an HMAC check over the raw body.

The browser elements, `<clipmux-uploader>` and `<clipmux-player>`, talk to
your own routes, so they work with a backend in any language.

## Before you start

- Your app's credentials. Approve the app with
  `npx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com` from any
  folder (it needs Node, but your backend doesn't), or on the server run
  `clipmux admin create-integration --app NAME --webhook-url URL >> .env`.
  Either way you get `CLIPMUX_URL`, `CLIPMUX_API_KEY`,
  `CLIPMUX_SIGNING_KID`, `CLIPMUX_SIGNING_KEY` and
  `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- Keep all but `CLIPMUX_URL` on your server, out of browser code and logs.

## Call the API

Every call goes to the server's public URL with the API key as a bearer
token:

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/app \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY"
```

`GET /v1/app` returns your app, its scopes, the media origin (`base_url`)
and the longest token lifetime. A key's default scopes are `uploads:write`,
`assets:read` and `assets:write`. Requests and responses are JSON, and an
error is `{"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}` with a stable `code`.

Every `POST` takes an `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry with the same key
and the same request returns the first response, so a network error never
makes a second upload:

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/uploads \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: lesson_42' \
  -d '{"size": 10485760, "passthrough": "lesson_42", "title": "Lesson 42"}'
```

A `429 rate_limited` carries `Retry-After` in seconds; wait that long and
retry.

### The OpenAPI spec

The server describes its integration API, delivery URLs and webhooks as
OpenAPI 3.1 at `GET /openapi.json`, with no credential:

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/openapi.json -o clipmux-openapi.json
```

Generate a client from it with your language's OpenAPI tools, or browse it
in the [API reference](/docs/reference/api).

## Uploads from the browser

`<clipmux-uploader create-url="/your/route">` POSTs `{"size", "name",
"type"}` to your route, with the page's cookies. Your route checks the user,
calls `POST /v1/uploads` with its API key, and answers with ClipMux's
response plus one field, `endpoint`, set to your `CLIPMUX_URL`:

```json
{
  "upload_id": "upl_…",
  "asset_id": "ast_…",
  "part_size": 33554432,
  "part_count": 1,
  "upload_token": "…",
  "playback_ids": [{ "id": "pid_…", "policy": "signed", "playable": false, "status": "active" }],
  "endpoint": "https://video.example.com"
}
```

The browser then sends the file in parts straight to storage with the
`upload_token`, which reaches only that upload. Answer `401` or `403` to
refuse. See [Upload from the browser](/docs/build/upload/browser).

## Playback

For `<clipmux-player>`, give it your own token route with `getToken`, or a
route that answers its `session-url` POST. Either way your route checks the
viewer and signs a token. The signing code for Python, Go and PHP is in
[Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens); the player's side is
in [Add the player](/docs/build/play/player).

## Webhooks

Verify each webhook over the raw body with your `whsec_…` secret, then
re-fetch the video with `GET /v1/assets/{id}` before you store anything.
The verifying code for Python, Go and PHP, and the test vectors to check
your own, are in
[Verify webhook signatures](/docs/build/webhooks/verify-signatures). To
receive webhooks on your laptop, run `clipmux listen`; see
[Develop locally with listen](/docs/build/webhooks/listen).

## Check it works

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://video.example.com/v1/app \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY"
```

- `200`: the key works.
- `401 unauthorized`: the key is wrong or revoked.
- `403 insufficient_scope` on a later call: the key lacks that call's
  scope.

Then follow [Your first video with curl](/docs/build/first-video) from
upload to playback.
